meet.speaker: Clockmaker
text: Tick. Tock. Ah — a visitor with a heartbeat! Wonderful. Terrible timing, though.
The Big Clock has stopped. I've lost a gear — brass, about so big, very sentimental.
Since it stopped, the whole village keeps forgetting what time it is. Yesterday we had breakfast four times.

accept.speaker: Clockmaker
accept.text: Splendid! I last had it on a walk through the forest. East side, behind the old trees. Probably.

rude.speaker: Clockmaker
text: If you change your mind, I'll be here. Not that I'd know how long.

waiting.speaker: Clockmaker
waiting.text: Any luck? East side of the forest, behind the old trees. I can practically hear it ticking.

early.speaker: Clockmaker
text: Is that... my GEAR? In your hand? Without me even asking?
You're either very kind or very nosy. Either way: thank you!

return.speaker: Clockmaker
return.text: My gear! Oh, you wonderful, heartbeat-having person.

fix.speaker: Clockmaker
text: Listen to that. Lanternrest remembers what time it is!
Here — a Steady Lantern. It never flickers, no matter how dark the path. You'll want it if you're heading north.

ask.speaker: Clockmaker
text: One more thing. A clock that ticks in one place is a sad clock.
Would you take an old tinkerer along? I'm good with puzzles. And time. Mostly time.

wary.speaker: Clockmaker
text: ...Your hands have that dust on them. Lostling dust.
I think I'll stay with my clock. Clocks don't judge. Much.

joined.speaker: Clockmaker
joined.text: Splendid! Let me grab my second-best screwdriver. (The Clockmaker can slow time when summoned.)

stay.speaker: Clockmaker
stay.text: Ha! Very well. Someone has to remember the time.

after_wary.speaker: Clockmaker
after_wary.text: Tick, tock. The clock works fine. Thank you for that, at least.

after_ask.speaker: Clockmaker
after_ask.text: Back again! Changed your mind about company?
